title: Hypnos: Memory Efficient Homomorphic Processing Unit
problem: FHE accelerators traditionally use Host+ACC topology assuming encrypted data already resides on-chip, neglecting PCIe bus inefficiency and memory access overhead; this leads to poor end-to-end performance dominated by data movement rather than computation.
motivation: Fully Homomorphic Encryption enables privacy-preserving computation on encrypted data, but FHE's computational intensity and data volume create a critical memory-movement bottleneck in current accelerator designs.
method: Hypnos simplifies fully homomorphic encryption operations (computation on encrypted data) into memory-efficient commands. It pairs these with a paged memory management system—like how computers use virtual memory—that intelligently stages encrypted data between main memory and on-chip caches based on homomorphic encryption's irregular data access patterns. This approach eliminates the constant data movement and waiting time that slows down older accelerators, which assume all encrypted data must stay on-chip.
key_novelty: Hypnos introduces a paged memory management system designed for homomorphic encryption's irregular data access patterns, which stages data between off-chip and on-chip storage only when needed instead of requiring everything on-chip.
contributions: FHE operator abstraction into memory-efficient command streams
Paged memory management system for FHE-specific data access patterns
Architecture optimizing on-chip cache and memory hierarchy for FHE
2.58x speedup vs. SOTA ASIC, 4.43x vs. FPGA; 3.78x communication reduction; 27.6x-19.06x energy efficiency gain

metrics.energy_efficiency: 27.6x vs CraterLake ASIC, 19.06x vs Poseidon FPGA for ResNet-20

limitations: Not discussed; focus is on memory-efficiency optimization.
primary_theme: Memory-efficient FHE accelerator via paged management and operator abstraction
